definitions.explanation: A strength-training exercise in which one hangs from a bar and pulls oneself up until the chin is above the bar. A standard fitness exercise.
The state of being suspended or hanging from something. Used in technical or descriptive contexts.

examples.japanese: {懸垂|けんすい}を{十|じゅっ}{回|かい}やった。
{懸垂|けんすい}が{一|いっ}{回|かい}もできない。
examples.english: I can't do even a single pull-up.

examples.japanese: {毎日|まいにち}{公園|こうえん}の{鉄棒|てつぼう}で{懸垂|けんすい}のトレーニングをしている。
examples.english: I train pull-ups every day on the horizontal bar in the park.

examples.japanese: {懸垂|けんすい}{幕|まく}が{建物|たてもの}に{掛|か}かっている。
examples.english: A hanging banner is draped on the building.

examples.japanese: {橋|はし}の{懸垂|けんすい}{構造|こうぞう}が{美|うつく}しい。
examples.english: The suspension structure of the bridge is beautiful.

examples.japanese: {懸垂|けんすい}{式|しき}のモノレールは{線路|せんろ}の{下|した}にぶら{下|さ}がって{走|はし}る。
examples.english: A suspended monorail runs hanging below the track.

notes:
Composed of {懸|けん} (suspend/hang) + {垂|すい} (droop/hang down). The exercise meaning (sense 1) is the most commonly encountered usage in everyday conversation. Can also function as a する verb ({懸垂|けんすい}する).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {懸垂|けんすい}をする: to do pull-ups
- {懸垂|けんすい}{幕|まく}: hanging banner/vertical banner
- {懸垂|けんすい}{式|しき}: suspended type (e.g., monorail)
- {逆|さか}{手|て}{懸垂|けんすい}: chin-up (underhand grip)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- チンニング: chinning — English loanword alternative for pull-ups, used in gyms
- {鉄棒|てつぼう}: horizontal bar — the equipment used for pull-ups (also a gymnastics apparatus)
